Close Spring Studio and prepare the next teaching cycle

You are Rivergate Performing Arts Conservatory's operations and finance lead. The conservatory teaches public workshops and corporate groups, using its teaching artists, hired rooms and an accompanist agency. The April–June Spring Studio quarter has ended, but its records do not yet agree on which teaching took place or what remains payable. Today is 30 June 2027. Close the quarter and confirm the next cycle's arrangements. Amounts are USD and times are UTC.

Attendance exports contain missing and duplicate rows, and some classes were moved or cancelled. These changes affect public enrolments, corporate invoices, artist fees and room charges. One posted learner refund also lacks a matching cancellation. Establish the delivered work from the supplied evidence, then bring the related records into agreement. A learner's absence from a delivered class is not a cancellation.

The next cycle includes a requested public workshop and two corporate renewal packages, including remote coaching. Their dates, rooms and artists must be confirmed before the conservatory commits its available cash. Signed choices, replacement offers and permitted deferrals are already supplied; no new external reply is needed.

Task materials

Use public/materials.json to find the original business evidence by subject or business reference. It links to readable excerpts in public/business_materials.md and to their original Twenty notes. 

Twenty contains the original teaching, attendance, contract, bank and renewal evidence. Pretix holds public enrolments and refunds; BigCapital holds corporate invoices, supplier bills, credits and receipts; HRMS holds artists' duties, leave and expense claims. Use public/records.json and the original native-ID maps to locate records. Full business conditions are in public/business_policy.md, and public/recording.md defines the seven linked closeout tables.

Required outcomes

- Establish the teaching actually delivered this quarter from the delivery, attendance and cancellation records, then bring public registrations and corporate charges into agreement with that work. Complete outstanding authorized cancellation refunds, make supported corporate billing corrections and reconcile the existing deposit to bank evidence. Preserve processed refunds and original receipt allocations, and create a dated recovery follow-up for the refund without a supported cancellation.
- Reconcile amounts owed to teaching artists, the accompanist agency and venues, and resolve employee expense claims. Artist fees and corrected duties must reflect actual teaching and preparation allowed by their contracts; supplier charges must reflect actual service and authorized remedies. Avoid counting shared journeys or supplier-billed costs twice, and implement the corresponding accounting adjustments and expense approvals without paying fees or reimbursements.
- Record each corporate client's signed renewal or closure decision and implement the requested public workshop and complete corporate renewal packages. Confirm suitable rooms and qualified, available teaching artists in visible Twenty calendars and submitted HRMS duties. Remote coaching also needs a scheduled time and artist, but no physical room. Preserve approved leave and other existing commitments.
- Using the reconciled obligations, including new room deposits, prepare settlement instructions by date and payee for 1–20 July. Follow contractual due dates and authorized deferrals, retaining the $5,000 operating reserve after every date. Distinguish instructions supported by current funds, authorized deferred fees and later unfunded obligations. Credits and future collections are not cash; do not execute transfers or payroll.

Make the required changes in the applications and complete the handover under the policy and recording guides. Preserve original evidence and unrelated records. Keep future activities recorded as arrangements rather than completed work. You may organize the work freely.

Close the league round and arrange the next fixtures

You work in Ridgeway Amateur League's finance and operations team. The regional seven-a-side league has completed its September round and is preparing the next fixtures for 9–16 October. Today is 1 October 2027. Resolve the completed round's accounts and confirm the next round's arrangements. Amounts are USD and times are UTC.

The league charges teams for administration and player places, while some players pay their entries individually. Transfers, replacements and duplicate roster imports have left those records out of agreement with the actual registrations. Some fixtures and contracted services were also disrupted, affecting pitch and equipment charges and the advertising promised to sponsors. Each account needs to reflect the service and remedies supported by its own agreement.

The league's referees and coordinators have unpaid fees and travel claims from the round. Alongside those existing obligations, the next fixtures require accepted pitches and available, qualified officials. The recorded team choices and supplier offers are already available; the remaining work is to reconcile the accounts, confirm the future bookings and staffing, and fit the resulting obligations within available funds.

Task materials

Use public/materials.json to find the original business evidence by subject or business reference. It links to readable excerpts in public/business_materials.md and to their original Twenty notes. 

Twenty notes titled Ridgeway Amateur League — ... contain the signed charging agreement, team-place and entry registers, match sheets, advertising evidence, next-round offers and cash authority. Pretix holds individual entries and payments; BigCapital holds team, sponsor and supplier accounts; HRMS holds officials' claims, qualifications, leave and duties. Use public/records.json and the native-ID maps to locate records. Full rules and seven handover formats are in public/business_policy.md and public/recording.md.

Required outcomes

- Reconcile team charges and individual entries to the verified rosters, delivered services and authorized transfers. Apply supported credits to original invoices while preserving administration fees and receipt allocations. Complete the expressly authorized Pretix entry cancellations and original-payment refunds; retain nonrefundable entries and do not refund duplicate imports or undocumented replacements.
- Resolve the league's pitch, equipment and sponsor accounts using actual performance, notice and accepted remedies. Apply supported supplier credits while retaining legitimate minimum charges, and retain the advertising services and signed alternatives already delivered.
- Determine the officials' unpaid fees and resolve their expense claims from actual work, travel, receipts and contractual caps. Count shared journeys once and exclude directly billed or company-paid costs. Approve and submit supported HRMS claims without treating the fee ledger as payroll or paying reimbursements.
- Confirm the complete next round in pitch/time windows accepted by both teams. Provide a qualified, available referee and coordinator for each fixture, with visible Twenty calendars and matching HRMS duties. Include the selected hire costs and respect occupied pitches, capacity, leave and existing work.
- Prepare dated settlement instructions covering the reconciled obligations, next-round hire and authorized entry refunds. Use actual funds and only the documented vendor deferral, retaining at least $6,000 after each date. Future collections and credits are not cash. Apart from the required entry refunds, do not execute bank transfers or payroll.

Make the required changes in the applications and complete the handover under the policy and recording guides. Preserve original evidence and unrelated records. Keep future activities recorded as arrangements rather than completed work. You may organize the work freely.

Reconcile the October service accounts and arrange the remaining work

You work in Northwind Managed Services' finance and operations team. The company carries out implementation projects for business clients and provides ongoing support under separate agreements. Today is 1 November 2027. Close the October service accounts and confirm the remaining remediation and support work for 4–12 November. Amounts are USD and times are UTC.

A subcontractor failed to deliver part of its work, and some customer acceptance remains disputed. The amount chargeable to a client depends on the project work actually accepted or the support service provided. Supplier bills and employee travel claims need their own review, and sales commissions must follow each plan's terms for eligible charges and collections. Existing remittances and bank evidence show which customer payments have already been received.

There is also agreed customer work still to arrange, including remediation visits and continuing support. It needs qualified employees in the accepted customer windows, with purchased support available where authorized. The final handover must connect corrected customer and supplier positions, staff and commission obligations, and the cost of the selected future arrangements to a funded payment schedule.

Required outcomes

- Reconcile each client's implementation and support charges against the signed terms and actual acceptance or service evidence. Treat separately priced work, support usage and authorized travel recharges according to their own agreements, and apply supported corrections to the original accounts. Match existing receipts to remittances and bank evidence without posting money again or changing their allocations; planned remediation is not accepted work.
- Resolve subcontractor bills and employee claims from the work performed, approved costs and original receipts. Apply the documented supplier credits while retaining performed service charges, avoid duplicate and company-paid expenses, and approve and submit supported HRMS claims without paying them.
- Use the corrected customer positions and each signed sales plan to determine which commissions are earned, deferred, cancelled or offset. Apply the required collection conditions, record the resulting unpaid amounts and do not claim that payroll or commission recovery has occurred.
- Confirm the outstanding remediation visits and continuing-support arrangements in full. Cover every session in its accepted customer windows, assigning qualified available employees for internal delivery or selecting the specifically authorized supplier offer. Record visible calendars and, for internal sessions, matching HRMS duties; preserve leave and existing work, and include any selected supplier cost in the handover.

Use the actual bank balance and the documented support-bill deferral, retaining $15,000 after each date. Credits and expected collections are not cash; do not execute transfers or payroll.

Reconcile disrupted workspace services and arrange replacement access

You work in Harborline Workspaces' finance and operations team. The company provides office access to members and rents meeting rooms separately. Water damage, delayed electrical work and a chiller failure disrupted October's service. Today is 1 November 2027. Resolve the affected accounts and confirm the replacement-access and reopening arrangements needed for 4–12 November. Amounts are USD and times are UTC.

Some customers used accepted replacement space; others lost contracted access. Membership agreements define which access losses qualify for a credit against issued unpaid November invoices. Separately billed rooms have their own signed correction destinations; paid October history remains intact. The company also needs to check what it owes the repair contractors and landlords, and which employee expenses are supported by actual service and payment evidence.

The next arrangements must accommodate customers in available internal desks or accepted partner premises while maintenance and reopening work proceed. Those choices create further commitments alongside the existing payables. The task is to leave customer remedies, space and staffing bookings, supplier balances and the payment plan in agreement with the company's actual funds.

Keep membership access and separately billed meeting rooms distinct, retain genuine delivered-service and cancellation charges, and apply authorized credits to the unpaid invoice named in each signed correction. Preserve paid October history; do not replace the agreed credit remedy with cash refunds or deposit transactions.
- Reconcile maintenance and landlord charges to authorized work actually performed and written remedies. Correct unsupported charges while preserving legitimate bills and payments. Resolve employee claims using original receipts and reimbursement rules, excluding shared or company-paid costs already counted elsewhere, and submit supported approvals without paying them.

Follow their due dates and the signed vendor deferral, using actual cash and retaining at least $40,000 after each date. Credits and expected collections cannot fund payments, and the instructions must remain unexecuted.

Make the required changes in the applications and complete the handover under the policy and recording guides. Preserve original evidence and unrelated records. Keep future activities recorded as arrangements rather than completed work. You may organize the work freely.

Reconcile Stonebridge's hire accounts and confirm its next jobs

You work in Stonebridge Machinery Hire's finance and operations team. The company rents machinery to customers and uses its own mechanics and outside workshops to service it. Today is 1 November 2027. Reconcile the recent hire accounts and confirm the signed requests for the next jobs. Amounts are USD and times are UTC.

Recent hires involved delays, breakdowns, replacement machines, damage and late returns. Customer charges must follow the hire agreements, while workshop and mobile-service bills must reflect the work authorized and performed. Mechanics have filed draft expense claims, and some customer business came through resellers with separate commission agreements. These are different amounts owed by or to the company, supported by their own records.

The next hire jobs already have accepted alternatives for equipment or transport runs and customer time windows. They still need available capacity and qualified leads to be booked. Those bookings carry costs, so the final account positions, earned reseller fees, employee reimbursements and selected future offers must be brought into one payment plan using actual funds.

Apply supported credits to original invoices and match existing customer payments to bank and remittance evidence. Preserve issued amounts and allocations; a supplier's replacement cost is not automatically chargeable to the customer.
- Resolve workshop and mobile-service bills against authorized work, contractual minimums and supported remedies. Check the mechanics' jobs so internal and external services are attributed correctly. Finalize and submit employee claims from their original receipts and actual payers, excluding duplicate or unsupported costs and leaving approved reimbursements unpaid.

Do not count credits or expected receipts as cash, or execute payments, payroll or transfers.

Reconcile Pinewater's laboratory accounts and arrange the next sampling work

You work in Pinewater Commercial Testing's finance and operations team. Pinewater tests customers' samples, sends some analyses to outside laboratories and uses couriers to move samples. Today is 1 November 2027. Resolve the recent testing accounts and confirm the signed requests for the next sampling appointments. Amounts are USD and times are UTC.

The billing records do not consistently reflect what samples were accepted, what tests were completed or who was responsible for rejected or delayed work. Rush orders and repeat tests have their own terms. Customer corrections must be considered separately from outside-laboratory and courier charges; technicians' actual travel costs and fees owed to referral partners also need checking under their respective agreements.

The next sampling work has agreed customer windows and offered sampling-vehicle slots. It still needs qualified staff and available transport capacity to be reserved. The company must cover the corrected existing obligations and selected future bookings from its actual funds, leaving a consistent account, appointment, staffing and payment handover without claiming the future samples have already been collected.

Close Copperline's campaign accounts and arrange its next production work

Today is 1 November 2027. Resolve the recent campaign accounts and confirm the signed requests for upcoming shoots and edits. Amounts are USD and times are UTC.

Clients accept different film components separately and may use them only within the rights purchased. The existing accounts need to be checked against that acceptance and use, and against the costs clients authorized the company to recharge. Supplier bills, staff expense claims and intermediary fees remain separate obligations: a client recharge limit does not cancel a genuine supplier cost, and a personal reimbursement is not another client sale.

Future work already has accepted customer windows and studio or production-slot offers. The company must reserve suitable capacity and qualified producers or editors, then include those commitments alongside the reconciled accounts in its payment plan. Complete the developer source formatting engine

Implement the missing source formatting subsystem in Black 25.1.0. Developers
need to format real Python modules consistently, without changing their meaning,
and integrate formatting into file, stdin and API workflows. The supplied parser,
syntax-tree primitives, options/modes, project discovery, cache and reporting
helpers are available; formatting and integration behavior are missing.

Five substantial responsibilities must work together:
1. Layout: build logical lines, track brackets and indentation, split long
   expressions/calls/collections, preserve trailing-comma semantics, remove
   unnecessary parentheses and apply the configured line length and blank lines.
2. Literals: normalize string quoting/prefixes, docstrings and numeric spelling
   without changing their values; respect string-normalization settings and
   supported optional string-transform features.
3. Comments: preserve attached comments, type comments and docstrings; honor
   fmt: off/on/skip regions and maintain correct comment placement during splits.
4. Syntax: format supported Python expressions, statements, decorators,
   annotations, comprehensions, async constructs and pattern matching. Infer
   or honor target grammar versions and feature-dependent formatting choices.
5. Integration: implement format_str/format_file_contents, file and stdin CLI
   workflows, check/diff/write behavior and encoding/newline preservation.
   Enforce semantic equivalence and stability in safe mode. Formatting already
   formatted output must be idempotent. Preserve public errors and CLI exits.

Notebook cell masking and daemon transport are supplied and outside the missing
scope. The import-time line splitting decorator, Mode, parser declarations and
generated version metadata remain supplied. Original public tests/docstrings
are retained. Implement behavior, not a private algorithm. Private grading sends
actual formatted programs to a fresh offline Python consumer with no Black or
source checkout and checks frozen upstream formatting expectations and execution.

Set PYTHONPATH=/work/project/src. Public checks:
/opt/engineering/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_format.py
CLI: /opt/engineering/bin/python -m black --check path/to/program.py

Complete the Python project build frontend

A release pipeline has Python, packaging, pyproject-hooks, pip and flit-core,
plus project source and build backends. Its build frontend implementation is
missing. Complete the public build 1.2.2 SDK and CLI over these provided tools.
The fixed source is commit 3b0b5d07077473f5da3f038cf7b74cd2b65d2a98.
This is an entire tool implementation. Module declarations, compatibility
imports, type aliases, error representations, ContextVar logging accessors and package identity remain.

1. Project configuration: validate source directories, parse TOML and the
build-system table, resolve source/interpreter paths, recognize legacy defaults
and reject malformed or unsupported table fields with meaningful public errors.
2. Backend orchestration: dispatch PEP 517 hooks with config settings, expose
backend requirements, prepare metadata, fall back to wheel metadata when the
optional hook is unavailable, preserve custom subprocess runners and wrap errors.
3. Release artifacts: build actual wheel and sdist files into absolute/relative
output directories, forward settings and prepared metadata, and support building
a wheel from an unpacked sdist. A successful message without usable files fails.
4. Isolation and dependencies: create and clean DefaultIsolatedEnv, use its
interpreter and environment with ProjectBuilder.from_isolated_env, install build
requirements through the supplied installer, and check missing/version/marker
requirements. Offline local-backend projects must work with empty requirements;
no external network access is required. Existing pip/uv and virtualenv interfaces
may be supported as described by the public source; the provided pip path is the
required offline environment path. Supply accurate diagnostics on failures.
5. CLI: implement python -m build option handling, wheel/sdist selection, default
sdist-then-wheel workflow, output paths, backend -C settings, dependency checking,
--no-isolation, logging and failure exit codes. Keep CLI and SDK behavior coherent.

Use /opt/engineering/bin/python with PYTHONPATH=/work/project/src for public
checks. Original tests and example backends are provided. You may introduce
helpers while preserving public entrypoints. pip, pytest, packaging and
pyproject-hooks are infrastructure; no installed build frontend is supplied.
Build your frontend wheel with:
  PYTHONPATH=src /opt/engineering/bin/python -c 'from flit_core.buildapi import build_wheel; build_wheel("dist")'
Create dist first. Submit the editable source. Independent grading builds your
SDK wheel and invokes it from a consumer without this checkout. It uses actual
local backend subprocesses, imported wheel code, archive contents, SDK exceptions,
CLI outcomes and environment cleanup. Private checks are not available tools.

Complete a local JSON Schema to Python model compiler

A service platform needs to deliver typed Python models from its versioned JSON
Schema contracts. Implement the missing JSON Schema compilation subsystem of
datamodel-code-generator. Consumers must be able to import the generated files
and validate data without installing or importing the generator.

Use the existing generate API and command-line interface. Inputs are local JSON
Schema documents, including locally referenced documents. Produce Pydantic v1
Python source using the provided formatter and templates. The CLI must support
--input, --input-file-type jsonschema, --output and --disable-timestamp.

Complete these substantial capabilities:
1. Schema semantics: object properties, required versus optional values, defaults,
   integer and string bounds, string patterns, array size and element constraints,
   date-time fields and additionalProperties=False. Valid data must be accepted;
   invalid data must be rejected by the generated Pydantic models.
2. References and dependencies: shared internal definitions, recursive object
   references, local external references, reusable model identity, import ordering
   and forward-reference resolution. Generated modules must import successfully
   in an environment with only Pydantic and its dependencies.
3. Model shapes: ordinary object models, unions of referenced object models,
   root enums, dictionaries and constrained arrays, and nullable values. Preserve
   the documented Pydantic parse_obj and serialization behavior.
4. Naming policy: Python-safe property names, snake_case_field, input aliases,
   explicit aliases and class_name overrides. Input keys and by_alias JSON
   serialization must preserve the schema contract, even if Python names differ.
5. Delivery: integrate the API and CLI with actual file output. Identical inputs
   and settings with timestamps disabled must generate identical source. Deliver
   standalone modules, not modules depending on this compiler's private classes.

Provided infrastructure includes CLI configuration, YAML loading, Python source
formatting, Pydantic schema declarations and model templates. The templates are
building blocks; parsing, reference/type resolution, model construction and
emission orchestration are missing. Import-time Pydantic registration is retained.
Keep the supplied YAML loader and CLI --help working. Other schema input formats,
network references and non-Pydantic backends are outside this task.

Workspace: /work/project. Python: /opt/engineering/bin/python.
Run public checks from the repository and exercise the API/CLI on your own local
schemas. Evaluation checks source-generated artifacts in a separate environment,
using valid and invalid payloads, reference identity and serialization behavior.

shipping source folders that only work in the development checkout. Complete
the missing Hatchling metadata and distribution-building subsystem through the
existing PEP 517 build_wheel/build_sdist interfaces and builder/plugin APIs.
Work with local projects; no registry upload or network service is required.

Complete these responsibilities:

# Upgrade document management with configurable lifecycle workflows

A document-management installation currently uses limited Consumption Templates. Operators need reusable workflows for intake routing, post-extraction classification and later document corrections, including metadata and access-policy assignment. Implement the integrated workflow product while preserving existing installations.

## Starting point

The original application, source and native tests are provided. Implement this upgrade in the repository using the existing architecture and public API conventions; your internal solution need not reproduce a hidden patch. Existing synthetic installation data is also provided for migration testing.

## Required product behavior

### Reusable workflow administration

Provide persistent workflows with names, enabled state, sort order, multiple triggers and ordered assignment actions. Support nested create/read/update/delete through /api/workflows/ and /api/workflows/{id}/, alongside workflow trigger/action endpoints. Validate references, trigger types, consumption filters and title placeholders. Consumption triggers require filename, path or mail-rule filters. Invalid updates must not corrupt saved definitions. Restrict administration to users granted application workflow permissions; workflows are globally shared definitions, not individually owned records.

### Source-aware document intake automation

Run enabled consumption-started workflows in sort order before ingestion applies document metadata. Match source, case-insensitive filename/path wildcards and optional mail rule. All applicable filters on a trigger must match; any applicable trigger can activate its workflow. Mail-rule filtering implies the mail-fetch source. Route an uploaded document through the actual ingestion pipeline, persisting assigned metadata and preserving nonmatching documents. Source/path information is used at consumption time, rather than fabricated after ingestion.

### Post-ingestion and document-update automation

Support Document Added and Document Updated triggers at their actual lifecycle stages. Match extracted content with none/any/all/literal/regex/fuzzy algorithms, case sensitivity, any of selected tags, document type and correspondent. Added triggers operate after extraction and ordinary matching. Updated triggers operate after document edits. Correctly apply the matching actions and save their resulting metadata; do not run mismatched trigger types or filters. Avoid recursive updates that prevent normal document editing.

### Ordered metadata and access-policy assignment

Assignment actions can set title, correspondent, document type, storage path, owner, tags, custom-field membership and view/edit permissions for users/groups. Support the documented title placeholders for each lifecycle stage. Execute workflow/action order consistently: later scalar assignments replace earlier values, while tags, custom fields and permissions merge without duplicate accumulation. Custom fields are attached without inventing a value. Disabled workflows do not apply. Persist owner/access changes so granted users can access documents and unrelated users cannot.

### Integrated workflow configuration interface

Extend the existing English web application with workflow management navigation, listing, create/edit/delete and enable controls. Provide editors for multiple triggers, filtering and assignment actions, with validation feedback. Saving through the interface must persist a usable definition that affects real document processing. Users without workflow administration permissions must not receive administrative access. Preserve the existing document interface.

### Existing-installation upgrade

Migrate existing Consumption Templates into enabled workflows, preserving order, source/filename/path/mail-rule filters and all metadata/permission assignments. Keep existing accounts, passwords, documents, tags and stored files intact. Grant workflow application permissions to existing users/groups with add-document permissions, while retaining superuser access. The resulting rules must still act on new intake. Repeated application startup must not duplicate converted rules or lose records.

## Public interface and compatibility

Preserve the existing /api/ document and metadata endpoints, token authentication via POST /api/token/ with username/password, and Authorization: Token <token>. Workflow API records contain id, name, order, enabled, triggers and actions. Triggers contain id, type (1 consumption started, 2 added, 3 updated), sources (1 consume folder, 2 API upload, 3 mail fetch), filter_filename, filter_path, filter_mailrule, matching_algorithm (0 none, 1 any word, 2 all words, 3 exact match, 4 regex, 5 fuzzy), match, is_insensitive, filter_has_tags, filter_has_correspondent and filter_has_document_type.
